q-qt-tag.label: Choose the question tag
q-qt-tag.summary: Match the auxiliary and the subject, and turn the polarity the other way.

rules.text: A positive statement takes a negative tag and a negative statement takes a positive one. The tag repeats the statement's auxiliary and replaces the subject with a pronoun: She is coming, isn't she?
rules.ok: She is coming, isn't she? He cannot swim, can he?
rules.bad: She is coming, is she? He cannot swim, cannot he?

rules.text: If the statement has no auxiliary, the tag uses do, does or did to match the tense: He works here, doesn't he? They left early, didn't they?
Words that are already negative in sense (never, hardly, scarcely, seldom, nobody, nothing, few, little) make the statement negative, so the tag is positive.
rules.ok: He hardly speaks, does he? Nothing was lost, was it?

rules.text: Three forms are fixed: 'Let us ...' takes 'shall we?', an imperative takes 'will you?', and 'I am ...' takes 'aren't I?'. 'Everyone', 'somebody' and 'nobody' are answered by 'they'.
rules.ok: Let us begin, shall we? Open the door, will you? I am late, aren't I? Everyone came, didn't they?
rules.bad: Let us begin, will we? I am late, amn't I?

q-qt-tag.cue: A statement followed by a comma and a blank at the very end of the sentence.
q-qt-tag.standard: Find the auxiliary (or supply do / does / did), flip the polarity, and put in the pronoun for the subject.
q-qt-tag.fast: Positive statement, negative tag; negative statement, positive tag. Then check the auxiliary.
q-qt-tag.eliminate: Drop every option whose polarity matches the statement, then every option with the wrong auxiliary.
traps: A hidden negative (hardly, never, nobody) which makes the statement negative.
An imperative takes 'will you' whatever its own verb is.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
She has finished the assignment, ___
practice.why: The statement is positive and its auxiliary is 'has', so the tag is the negative 'hasn't she?'.

a.note: The polarity is not turned: a positive statement needs a negative tag.

c.note: 'Doesn't' is used only when the statement has no auxiliary of its own; here it has 'has'.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
He works at the post office, ___
practice.why: There is no auxiliary in the statement, so the tag supplies 'does' for the present tense, in the negative.

b.note: 'Isn't he' assumes an auxiliary 'is', which the statement does not have.

d.note: 'Won't' puts the tag in the future, which the statement is not.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
They left before the interval, ___
practice.why: The statement is in the simple past with no auxiliary, so the tag takes 'didn't'.

a.note: 'Don't' is present; the statement is past.

d.note: 'Weren't' assumes an auxiliary 'were', which the statement does not have.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
He hardly ever complains, ___
practice.why: 'Hardly' makes the statement negative in sense, so the tag is positive: 'does he?'.

a.note: This treats the statement as positive, but 'hardly' has already made it negative.

c.note: 'Did' puts the tag in the past; the statement is in the present.

d.note: 'Isn't' changes the auxiliary and the polarity both.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
Nobody informed the warden, ___
practice.why: 'Nobody' is negative in sense, so the tag is positive, and 'nobody' is answered by 'they'.

a.note: This keeps the tag negative although 'nobody' has already made the statement negative.

c.note: The polarity is right but 'nobody' takes 'they', not 'he'.

d.note: Wrong on both counts: negative tag and the wrong pronoun.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
Let us start the meeting, ___
practice.why: 'Let us' takes the fixed tag 'shall we?'.

a.note: 'Will we' is the commonest wrong answer here; the fixed form is 'shall we'.

c.note: 'Don't we' does not follow a 'let us' sentence.

d.note: 'Shan't we' makes the tag negative, which 'let us' does not take.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
Shut the window, ___
practice.why: An imperative takes the fixed tag 'will you?'.

a.note: 'Won't you' is used as an invitation, not as the ordinary tag on a command.

c.note: 'Don't you' does not follow an imperative.

d.note: 'Shall you' is not used as a tag.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
I am next in the queue, ___
practice.why: 'I am' takes the fixed tag 'aren't I?'.

a.note: 'Amn't' is not a form used in English.

d.note: 'Isn't it' is used in Indian English for every statement, but the tag must match the subject 'I'.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
You cannot drive without a licence, ___
practice.why: The statement is negative, so the tag is positive and keeps the auxiliary 'can'.

b.note: This repeats the negative instead of turning it.

c.note: 'Do' replaces the auxiliary 'can', which the statement already has.

practice.text:
Select the correct question tag to complete the sentence.
Everyone has signed the register, ___
practice.why: 'Everyone' is answered by 'they', and the positive statement with 'has' takes the negative tag 'haven't they?'.

a.note: 'He' agrees with the singular verb but 'everyone' is answered by 'they' in a tag.

c.note: The polarity is not turned, and the pronoun is wrong.

d.note: 'Didn't' changes the tense from the present perfect to the past.
